k: Hush. Don't look so frightened, little lambs. It's only singing.
src: 'Hush. Don\'t look so frightened, little lambs. It\'s only singing.'

k: THE RINGING BELL — Rooms · Suppers · Songs.nNo rooks.
src: 'THE RINGING BELL — Rooms · Suppers · Songs.\nNo rooks.'

k: BELLWRIGHT ARMS & SUNDRIES — swords, salves and bell-bronze buckles.
src: 'BELLWRIGHT ARMS & SUNDRIES — swords, salves and bell-bronze buckles.'

k: THE LANTERN QUARTER.nResidents only after dusk. (We mean it.)
src: 'THE LANTERN QUARTER.\nResidents only after dusk. (We mean it.)'

k: LOW TOWN.nMind the mud. Mind your purse. Mind your business.
src: 'LOW TOWN.\nMind the mud. Mind your purse. Mind your business.'

k: The Grand Lantern of Aurenne, eldest of the Seven. Its light is so steady you can feel it on your face, like warm water.
src: 'The Grand Lantern of Aurenne, eldest of the Seven. Its light is so steady you can feel it on your face, like warm water.'

k: The door is barred with gold.
src: 'The door is barred with gold.'

k: It is humming. The same note as the forks.
src: 'It is humming. The same note as the forks.'

k: A fountain ringed with seven bronze lanterns. So many coins have been thrown in that the water runs copper-green.
src: 'A fountain ringed with seven bronze lanterns. So many coins have been thrown in that the water runs copper-green.'

k: St. Aurel, the first Keeper, holding up the first Lantern. Someone has tied a red ribbon round her wrist. Several someones, by the layers.
src: 'St. Aurel, the first Keeper, holding up the first Lantern. Someone has tied a red ribbon round her wrist. Several someones, by the layers.'

k: The Hierophant Cassian, carved in white marble. The sculptor gave him a gentler face than any statue has a right to.
src: 'The Hierophant Cassian, carved in white marble. The sculptor gave him a gentler face than any statue has a right to.'

k: Climb
src: 'Climb'

k: Grate
src: 'Grate'

k: A straw training dummy in a Dawnguard tabard. Someone has drawn a face on it. The face looks a great deal like Lord-Commander Garrick Thorne.
src: 'A straw training dummy in a Dawnguard tabard. Someone has drawn a face on it. The face looks a great deal like Lord-Commander Garrick Thorne.'

k: ...That's been there since my year. I didn't draw it. I would like that on the record.
src: '...That\'s been there since my year. I didn\'t draw it. I would like that on the record.'

k: Scratched into the drain-house wall at child height: four crowns, and under them, GUTTER CORT. One crown is fresh.
src: 'Scratched into the drain-house wall at child height: four crowns, and under them, GUTTER CORT. One crown is fresh.'

k: The river Aure, low and brown. A gull stands on a sandbar in the middle of it, looking personally betrayed.
src: 'The river Aure, low and brown. A gull stands on a sandbar in the middle of it, looking personally betrayed.'

k: Not while Nell and the others are down there.
src: 'Not while Nell and the others are down there.'

k: Not without Dad's compass.
src: 'Not without Dad\'s compass.'

k: The little ones are scrubbing my pots. Never seen pots so clean, or children so proud of it. Bed and supper, Page? Forty gold.
src: 'The little ones are scrubbing my pots. Never seen pots so clean, or children so proud of it. Bed and supper, Page? Forty gold.'

k: Welcome to the Ringing Bell! Bed, supper, and a bard who knows four songs. Forty gold.
src: 'Welcome to the Ringing Bell! Bed, supper, and a bard who knows four songs. Forty gold.'

k: the Ringing Bell
src: 'the Ringing Bell'

k: A song for the island folk? I know four. Three are about drinking. Here's the other one.
src: 'A song for the island folk? I know four. Three are about drinking. Here\'s the other one.'

k: ♪ _The festival lanterns were hung in a row, / and the Keeper's two children ran laughing below._ ♪
src: '♪ _The festival lanterns were hung in a row, / and the Keeper\'s two children ran laughing below._ ♪'

k: ♪ _Then the great light went out like a breath on a flame, / and the dark came to Aurenne and called them by name._ ♪
src: '♪ _Then the great light went out like a breath on a flame, / and the dark came to Aurenne and called them by name._ ♪'

k: ♪ _He held up the Lantern, the Keeper so true — / and the city was saved, and a girl was lost too._ ♪
src: '♪ _He held up the Lantern, the Keeper so true — / and the city was saved, and a girl was lost too._ ♪'

k: Not my best rhyme. The Choir doesn't care for it, so naturally it's the one everybody asks for.
src: 'Not my best rhyme. The Choir doesn\'t care for it, so naturally it\'s the one everybody asks for.'

k: Off duty. Which means I'm not here, and you didn't see me.
src: 'Off duty. Which means I\'m not here, and you didn\'t see me.'

k: If the Lord-Commander asks, I'm on patrol. This tankard is the patrol.
src: 'If the Lord-Commander asks, I\'m on patrol. This tankard is the patrol.'

k: Wait. Kestrel? Venn's squire? Dawn, man, everyone said you went soft on some island.
src: 'Wait. Kestrel? Venn\'s squire? Dawn, man, everyone said you went soft on some island.'

k: I went _salty._ It's different.
src: 'I went _salty._ It\'s different.'

k: The Ringing Bell has the best stew in the city. It's also the only stew in the city that's never made anyone ill.
src: 'The Ringing Bell has the best stew in the city. It\'s also the only stew in the city that\'s never made anyone ill.'

k: These are related facts.
src: 'These are related facts.'

k: Marta says I can have pie if I scrub ALL the pots. I've scrubbed all the pots twice.
src: 'Marta says I can have pie if I scrub ALL the pots. I\'ve scrubbed all the pots twice.'

k: Is it pie time? It feels like pie time.
src: 'Is it pie time? It feels like pie time.'

k: I don't remember being down there. Nell says that's good.
src: 'I don\'t remember being down there. Nell says that\'s good.'

k: I can do bows now. On my shoes. Pip showed me. Double-knots are for babies.
src: 'I can do bows now. On my shoes. Pip showed me. Double-knots are for babies.'

k: Marta says we can stay. Dishes for beds. She doesn't sing, I checked.
src: 'Marta says we can stay. Dishes for beds. She doesn\'t sing, I checked.'

k: Look after him, Fish-Bird. He thinks he's a prince. He's mostly just loud.
src: 'Look after him, Fish-Bird. He thinks he\'s a prince. He\'s mostly just loud.'

k: A brass bell over the bar. A card beneath it: RING FOR SERVICE. DON'T RING FOR FUN. WE MEAN YOU, TERRENCE.
src: 'A brass bell over the bar. A card beneath it: RING FOR SERVICE. DON\'T RING FOR FUN. WE MEAN YOU, TERRENCE.'

k: A pot of stew big enough to bathe in. It smells of rosemary and something brown and comforting.
src: 'A pot of stew big enough to bathe in. It smells of rosemary and something brown and comforting.'

k: Oswin
src: 'Oswin'

k: The Hierophant's Page! Going south? You'll want boots, water, and something sharp. I sell two of those.
src: 'The Hierophant\'s Page! Going south? You\'ll want boots, water, and something sharp. I sell two of those.'

k: Bellwright Arms & Sundries. Swords, salves, and the finest bell-bronze buckles in Aurenne.
src: 'Bellwright Arms & Sundries. Swords, salves, and the finest bell-bronze buckles in Aurenne.'

k: A bell-founder's anvil, cracked clean through. Oswin keeps it "for sentiment." There is a price tag on it anyway.
src: 'A bell-founder\'s anvil, cracked clean through. Oswin keeps it "for sentiment." There is a price tag on it anyway.'

k: Ledgers going back three generations of Bellwrights. The earliest entry: ONE (1) BELL, LARGE. PAID IN GEESE.
src: 'Ledgers going back three generations of Bellwrights. The earliest entry: ONE (1) BELL, LARGE. PAID IN GEESE.'

k: Imre
src: 'Imre'

k: His Holiness is waiting for you in his study, Page. The left-hand door.
src: 'His Holiness is waiting for you in his study, Page. The left-hand door.'

k: The Hierophant's study is through the left-hand door at the back. The archives, the right.
src: 'The Hierophant\'s study is through the left-hand door at the back. The archives, the right.'

k: Brother Quill keeps the archives. He is older than some of the books and fonder of them than of people.
src: 'Brother Quill keeps the archives. He is older than some of the books and fonder of them than of people.'

k: Welcome, pilgrim. The dawn-office is long over, but the light is always open.
src: 'Welcome, pilgrim. The dawn-office is long over, but the light is always open.'

k: I pray for my son every day. He's a sailor.
src: 'I pray for my son every day. He\'s a sailor.'

k: The Choir says the sea belongs to the Gloam after dark. So I pray very loudly at dusk.
src: 'The Choir says the sea belongs to the Gloam after dark. So I pray very loudly at dusk.'

k: Shh. I'm listening for the Dawnsong. You can hear it in here, if you're quiet.
src: 'Shh. I\'m listening for the Dawnsong. You can hear it in here, if you\'re quiet.'

k: ...You're not being quiet.
src: '...You\'re not being quiet.'

k: Sister Mercy's name has been struck from the rolls. I struck it myself. My hand would not stop shaking.
src: 'Sister Mercy\'s name has been struck from the rolls. I struck it myself. My hand would not stop shaking.'

k: Forty-one admitted. None discharged. How did none of us ever do the arithmetic?
src: 'Forty-one admitted. None discharged. How did none of us ever do the arithmetic?'

k: One Crest, one life, one light. It is carved under St. Aurel's feet. We say it every dawn.
src: 'One Crest, one life, one light. It is carved under St. Aurel\'s feet. We say it every dawn.'

k: I have said it eleven thousand times. I counted. That is my Crest, I think: Counter.
src: 'I have said it eleven thousand times. I counted. That is my Crest, I think: Counter.'

k: St. Aurel, holding up the first Lantern. Carved beneath her feet: *ONE CREST · ONE LIFE · ONE LIGHT.*
src: 'St. Aurel, holding up the first Lantern. Carved beneath her feet: *ONE CREST · ONE LIFE · ONE LIGHT.*'

k: A pillar carved with the Seven Lanterns, from Lanternfall in the west to Skyreach above the storm. Someone has rubbed Lanternfall's carving smooth with their thumb, over many years.
src: 'A pillar carved with the Seven Lanterns, from Lanternfall in the west to Skyreach above the storm. Someone has rubbed Lanternfall\'s carving smooth with their thumb, over many years.'

k: The Hierophant's study. The acolyte by the altar would know if you're expected.
src: 'The Hierophant\'s study. The acolyte by the altar would know if you\'re expected.'

k: A painting hangs on the wall beneath a white sheet. Not a speck of dust on it. Someone uncovers it often.
src: 'A painting hangs on the wall beneath a white sheet. Not a speck of dust on it. Someone uncovers it often.'

k: ...It's not ours to lift.
src: '...It\'s not ours to lift.'

k: Letters, stacked neatly on the desk. The one on top is in your own handwriting: your letter about the stars, from two winters ago.
src: 'Letters, stacked neatly on the desk. The one on top is in your own handwriting: your letter about the stars, from two winters ago.'

k: He kept it.
src: 'He kept it.'

k: An armillary sphere of brass rings. Where the little golden sun should sit at its center, there is only an empty socket.
src: 'An armillary sphere of brass rings. Where the little golden sun should sit at its center, there is only an empty socket.'

k: Treatises on the Dawnsong, scored and annotated in a fine hand. One spine has been read until it broke: *On the Inversion of Hymns.*
src: 'Treatises on the Dawnsong, scored and annotated in a fine hand. One spine has been read until it broke: *On the Inversion of Hymns.*'

k: Correspondence with the Keepers, filed by Lantern. The Lanternfall folder is very thin. On top, in Ysolde's hand, one word: NO.
src: 'Correspondence with the Keepers, filed by Lantern. The Lanternfall folder is very thin. On top, in Ysolde\'s hand, one word: NO.'

k: Search
src: 'Search'
